gaps.requirement: More than one spring powered device (code A4258) per 6 months is not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.source_sentence: More than one spring powered device (code A4258) per 6 months is not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule addresses a utilization limit for spring powered devices (A4258).

gaps.requirement: The medical necessity for a laser skin piercing device (code E0620) and related lens shield cartridge (code A4257) has not been established; therefore, claims for code E0620 and/or code A4257 will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.source_sentence: The medical necessity for a laser skin piercing device (code E0620) and related lens shield cartridge (code A4257) has not been established; therefore, claims for code E0620 and/or code A4257 will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule addresses denial of coverage for E0620 or A4257.

gaps.requirement: For a beneficiary who is not currently being treated with insulin administrations, up to 100 test strips and up to 100 lancets every 3 months are covered if the basic coverage criteria (1)-(2) (above) are met.
gaps.source_sentence: For a beneficiary who is not currently being treated with insulin administrations, up to 100 test strips and up to 100 lancets every 3 months are covered if the basic coverage criteria (1)-(2) (above) are met.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule specifies quantity limits for test strips and lancets for non-insulin treated beneficiaries.

gaps.requirement: For a beneficiary who is currently being treated with insulin administrations, up to 300 test strips and up to 300 lancets every 3 months are covered if basic coverage criteria (1)-(2) (above) are met.
gaps.source_sentence: For a beneficiary who is currently being treated with insulin administrations, up to 300 test strips and up to 300 lancets every 3 months are covered if basic coverage criteria (1)-(2) (above) are met.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule specifies quantity limits for test strips and lancets for insulin-treated beneficiaries.

gaps.requirement: For a beneficiary who is not currently being treated with insulin administrations, more than 100 test strips and more than 100 lancets every 3 months are covered if criteria (a) - (c) below are met.
gaps.source_sentence: For a beneficiary who is not currently being treated with insulin administrations, more than 100 test strips and more than 100 lancets every 3 months are covered if criteria (a) - (c) below are met.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule addresses high utilization criteria for non-insulin treated beneficiaries.

gaps.requirement: For a beneficiary who is currently being treated with insulin administrations, more than 300 test strips and more than 300 lancets every 3 months are covered if criteria (a) - (c) below are met.
gaps.source_sentence: For a beneficiary who is currently being treated with insulin administrations, more than 300 test strips and more than 300 lancets every 3 months are covered if criteria (a) - (c) below are met.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule addresses high utilization criteria for insulin-treated beneficiaries.

gaps.requirement: Lancets (code A4259), blood glucose test reagent strips (code A4253), glucose control solutions (code A4256) and spring powered devices for lancets (code A4258) are covered for beneficiaries for whom the glucose monitor is covered.
gaps.source_sentence: Lancets (code A4259), blood glucose test reagent strips (code A4253), glucose control solutions (code A4256) and spring powered devices for lancets (code A4258) are covered for beneficiaries for whom the glucose monitor is covered.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule explicitly ties coverage of these supplies to coverage of the glucose monitor.

gaps.requirement: Suppliers must not dispense a quantity of supplies exceeding a beneficiary's expected utilization. Suppliers must stay attuned to changed or atypical utilization patterns on the part of their clients. Suppliers must verify with the treating practitioner that any changed or atypical utilization is warranted.
gaps.source_sentence: Suppliers must not dispense a quantity of supplies exceeding a beneficiary's expected utilization. Suppliers must stay attuned to changed or atypical utilization patterns on the part of their clients. Suppliers must verify with the treating practitioner that any changed or atypical utilization is warranted.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule addresses supplier responsibility for monitoring and verifying atypical utilization.

gaps.requirement: Regardless of utilization, a supplier must not dispense more than a three (3) - month quantity of BGM testing supplies at a time.
gaps.source_sentence: Regardless of utilization, a supplier must not dispense more than a three (3) - month quantity of BGM testing supplies at a time.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule sets a maximum three-month supply limit for BGM testing supplies.

gaps.requirement: All therapeutic CGM devices billed to Medicare using HCPCS code K0554 must be reviewed for correct coding by the Pricing, Data Analysis and Coding (PDAC) contractor. Continuous Glucose Monitor systems that are billed using HCPCS code K0554, but that are not listed on the Product Classification List for HCPCS code K0554, will be denied as incorrect coding.
gaps.source_sentence: All therapeutic CGM devices billed to Medicare using HCPCS code K0554 must be reviewed for correct coding by the Pricing, Data Analysis and Coding (PDAC) contractor. Continuous Glucose Monitor systems that are billed using HCPCS code K0554, but that are not listed on the Product Classification List for HCPCS code K0554, will be denied as incorrect coding.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule requires PDAC review or Product Classification List inclusion for K0554 devices.

gaps.requirement: Proof of delivery (POD) is a Supplier Standard and DMEPOS suppliers are required to maintain POD documentation in their files. Proof of delivery documentation must be made available to the Medicare contractor upon request. All services that do not have appropriate proof of delivery from the supplier shall be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.source_sentence: Proof of delivery (POD) is a Supplier Standard and DMEPOS suppliers are required to maintain POD documentation in their files. Proof of delivery documentation must be made available to the Medicare contractor upon request. All services that do not have appropriate proof of delivery from the supplier shall be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule requires proof of delivery documentation.

gaps.requirement: For DMEPOS items and supplies provided on a recurring basis, billing must be based on prospective, not retrospective use. For DMEPOS products that are supplied as refills to the original order, suppliers must contact the beneficiary prior to dispensing the refill and not automatically ship on a pre-determined basis, even if authorized by the beneficiary. This shall be done to ensure that the refilled item remains reasonable and necessary, existing supplies are approaching exhaustion, and to confirm any changes or modifications to the order. Contact with the beneficiary or designee regarding refills must take place no sooner than 14 calendar days prior to the delivery/shipping date. For delivery of refills, the supplier must deliver the DMEPOS product no sooner than 10 calendar days prior to the end of usage for the current product. This is regardless of which delivery method is utilized.
gaps.source_sentence: For DMEPOS items and supplies provided on a recurring basis, billing must be based on prospective, not retrospective use. For DMEPOS products that are supplied as refills to the original order, suppliers must contact the beneficiary prior to dispensing the refill and not automatically ship on a pre-determined basis, even if authorized by the beneficiary. This shall be done to ensure that the refilled item remains reasonable and necessary, existing supplies are approaching exhaustion, and to confirm any changes or modifications to the order. Contact with the beneficiary or designee regarding refills must take place no sooner than 14 calendar days prior to the delivery/shipping date. For delivery of refills, the supplier must deliver the DMEPOS product no sooner than 10 calendar days prior to the end of usage for the current product. This is regardless of which delivery method is utilized.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule addresses refill timing, beneficiary contact, or prospective billing for recurring DMEPOS items.

gaps.requirement: For all DMEPOS items that are provided on a recurring basis, suppliers are required to have contact with the beneficiary or caregiver/designee prior to dispensing a new supply of items. Suppliers must not deliver refills without a refill request from a beneficiary. Items delivered without a valid, documented refill request will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.source_sentence: For all DMEPOS items that are provided on a recurring basis, suppliers are required to have contact with the beneficiary or caregiver/designee prior to dispensing a new supply of items. Suppliers must not deliver refills without a refill request from a beneficiary. Items delivered without a valid, documented refill request will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.
gaps.why_uncovered: No existing rule requires supplier contact or a documented refill request before dispensing recurring supplies.
